title: Event Shape Guardian: tenant-aware runtime validator and graceful-fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Redwood's usage analytics pipeline currently relies on a coarse-grained schema gate in the ingest layer that rejects malformed events outright. As we onboard more product teams and third-party integrations, we see two failure modes: (1) transient client-side shape drift causing downstream analytic gaps and dropped events; (2) tenant-specific optional fields (customer feature flags) that are valid for some customers but treated as invalid for others.

Goal:
Implement a tenant-aware runtime validation layer (Event Shape Guardian) that: (a) enforces required contracts for routing/crediting while allowing soft-acceptance for unknown/extra fields; (b) supports per-tenant schema overrides and compatibility rules; (c) provides deterministic transformation hooks for graceful conversion (e.g., rename/flatten) and automated canarying; (d) emits rich telemetry for validation rejection causes and conversion decisions.

Proposed solution overview:
- Introduce a new validation service deployed beside ingress (k8s autoscaled stateless pods).
- Validation rules stored in a versioned schema registry (S3-backed + Dynamo index) keyed by tenant_id, event_type, and schema_version. Registry entries include: required fields, allowed extras policy (ALLOW | WARN | REJECT), transformation snippets (JS/wasm limited DSL), and compatibility matrix.
- Runtime flow: HTTP/gRPC -> ingress adapter -> Event Shape Guardian -> canonicalizer -> Kafka topic (validated-stream) -> downstream consumers. Guardian returns fast 2xx with validation metadata header for soft-accepts; hard REJECTs return 422 with structured error.
- Soft-accept path: when policy=ALLOW or WARN, guardian stores original payload in raw-store (short TTL) and emits a validation_event to sidecar topic with metadata for downstream enrichment.
- Canary/rollout: support per-tenant canary flags (percent routing to strict mode) configurable from Console.
- Backpressure & replay: guardian can respond with 429 when downstream validated-stream lag exceeds threshold; ingestion adapter will buffer and backoff.
- Observability: per-tenant metrics (validation_rate, soft_accept_rate, hard_reject_rate), histogram of validation latency, example-sampling (presigned S3 links) for top error classes.

Implementation details / tech choices:
- Validation engine: use a WASM sandbox to run safe, precompiled conversion/normalization modules (faster and safer than eval'd JS). Write a small Rust shim that exposes a deterministic API (get_field, set_field, rename, drop).
- Schema representation: adopt JSON-Schema subset + custom policies; store canonical schema and a compatibility matrix. Use content-hash-based versioning to make caching simple.
- Storage: schema registry in S3 + Dynamo index for quick lookup; raw-store in S3 (30d TTL) for debugging with link references in validation events.
- Performance: aim for 99th perc latency < 120ms on p95 16k RPM baseline traffic. Add a local in-memory LRU cache for the last 5k tenant-schema combos; warm caches on deploy.
- Security: signer for transformation modules, validate module signatures at load-time; KMS-encrypted registry metadata. Security review required for module execution path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Guardian successfully validates and forwards events for 5 internal tenants with ENABLED soft-accept policies without increasing p95 latency > 1.25x baseline.
- Hard reject rate for production tenants is < 0.1% after 2 weeks of monitoring (post-rollout adjustments allowed).
- Console integration: UI toggles for per-tenant policy (ALLOW/WARN/REJECT) and percent canary control are available in the release (console-2026.04).
- Telemetry: dashboards showing validation_rate and top rejection reasons per tenant; alert for sudden spike > 5x baseline.

Rollout plan:
1) Development: implement registry proto, wasm runtime shim, and a prototype guardian in staging (2 weeks).
2) Canary: enable for internal tenants (team-internal) with WARN policy (2 weeks), iterate on transform modules.
3) Gradual expansion: enable soft-accept for low-traffic external tenants (percent canary ramp) and monitor metrics for 4 weeks.
4) Strict mode: after confidence, flip policy to REJECT where appropriate and deprecate tolerant transforms.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- DSL vs full WASM: DSL would be simpler for product teams but harder to express complex conversions; chosen path is WASM with a constrained standard library and signing.
- Storage TTL for raw-store: 30d is the initial value; may be expensive for large payloads — consider configurable per-tenant TTL.
- Who writes transform modules? Propose a small internal ops role + developer self-service through a signed upload process.

2026-03-02 — PM feedback (Lina Chen): require Console controls for per-tenant policy and canary percent; added as UI ticket to project backlog.
2026-03-03 — Infra note (Rajiv Kapoor): recommend a separate autoscaling policy group for validation pods to avoid eviction under cluster pressure; will provide HPA yaml.
2026-03-04 — Security (Nadia Gomez): approved running WASM sandboxes if we enforce signature verification and limit host APIs; security review scheduled 2026-03-10.
2026-03-05 — Decision: use S3 + Dynamo registry; implement in-memory LRU cache and expose stats via StatsD + Prometheus exporter. Added estimate bump to 8 points.
